                            (ny, nx) not in seen and grid[ny][nx] == color):
                        seen.add((ny, nx))
                        stack.append((ny, nx))

            top = min(y for y, x in cells)
            bottom = max(y for y, x in cells)
            left = min(x for y, x in cells)
            right = max(x for y, x in cells)
            shape = set(cells)

            # Mark as hollow when an interior zero is enclosed by the shape.
            outside = set()
            queue = []
            for y in range(top, bottom + 1):
                for x in range(left, right + 1):
                    if ((y, x) not in shape and
                            (y == top or y == bottom or x == left or x == right)):
                        outside.add((y, x))
                        queue.append((y, x))

            while queue:
                y, x = queue.pop()
                for ny, nx in ((y - 1, x), (y + 1, x),
                               (y, x - 1), (y, x + 1)):
                    if (top <= ny <= bottom and left <= nx <= right and
                            (ny, nx) not in shape and (ny, nx) not in outside):
                        outside.add((ny, nx))
                        queue.append((ny, nx))

            hollow = any(
                (y, x) not in shape and (y, x) not in outside
                for y in range(top + 1, bottom)
                for x in range(left + 1, right)
            )
            objects.append((cells, color, hollow, top, bottom))

    out = [[0] * w for _ in range(h)]
    occupied = set()

    # Hollow objects move up, while solid objects move down.
    for upward in (False, True):
        group = [obj for obj in objects if obj[2] == upward]

        step = -1 if upward else 1

        for cells, color, _, _, _ in group:
            shift = 0
            while True:
                candidate = [(y + shift + step, x) for y, x in cells]
                if any(y < 0 or y >= h or (y, x) in occupied
                       for y, x in candidate):
                    break
                shift += step

            for y, x in cells:
                ny = y + shift
                out[ny][x] = color
                occupied.add((ny, x))

    return out
